Surgery Information.Surgery Procedure: right breast mass removal with axillary lymph node dissection
Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: 1 cm, grade 1, infiltrating ductal carcinoma with clear surgical margins and 21 axillary lymph nodes were negative for metastatic carcinoma

Additional Comments: The patient has a history of osteoarthritis in the left hand, trace emphysema, diverticulosis, osteopenia, and a benign thyroid nodule. She experiences significant neuropathy in the right hand associated with a right brachial plexopathy and loss of muscle mass, dating back to a scalene rib removal in 1987 for thoracic outlet syndrome. She also has mild distal polyneuropathy with tingling and numbness in her feet and hands, which is somewhat improved with CoQ10. Additionally, she has short-term memory loss, a history of a small right frontal CVA in 2003, ocular migraines, and episodic dizziness and lightheadedness leading to falls. She has a history of hairline fractures in her wrists and elbows from falls, and a more recent ankle fracture requiring a brace. Her bone density in February 2008 revealed osteoporosis in her spine and osteopenia in her femur. She has been started on zoledronic acid for her osteoporosis and is being considered for aromatase inhibitor therapy.
